PLAINTIFE’S REPLY IN SUPPORT OF HIS MOTION FOR LEAVE
TO FILE A SUPPLEMENTAL COMPLAINT UNDER RULE 15(d)

I. NCMEC OPPOSES A CLAIM PLAINTIFF DID NOT PLEAD

Plaintiff’s proposed supplement states its purpose on its face. The August 12 filing and the
August 13 communication are not independent causes of action. Plaintiff pleads them as post-
filing facts. They bear on Count III. Count III already exists. Plaintiff said so in the pleading
NCMEC opposes.

NCMEC reads that pleading otherwise. Most of its Opposition explains why the August 12
filing and the August 13 communication do not create liability on their own. Plaintiff does not
dispute that. Plaintiff never pleaded it. NCMEC answers an argument Plaintiff did not make.

Remove that argument, and little of the Opposition remains. The supplement adds no

defendant. The supplement adds no cause of action. The supplement adds no category of relief.

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document 35 _ Filed 08/26/26 Page 2 of 4 PagelD# 376

The events occurred on August 12 and August 13. Plaintiff moved on August 20. NCMEC
identifies no prejudice. NCMEC identifies no delay. NCMEC identifies no discovery to reopen.
NCMEC identifies no deadline to disturb. NCMEC invokes futility. NCMEC never measures the
supplemental allegations against Count III.

NCMEC’s final substantive paragraph completes the error. NCMEC argues that the
supplement does not inform Plaintiff’s claim that NCMEC “defamed Plaintiff by imputation.”
Count III is not a defamation claim. Count III is the only count Plaintiff seeks to supplement.
NCMEC analyzed a count Plaintiff did not move to supplement.

NCMEC therefore opposes a claim Plaintiff did not plead. NCMEC opposes that claim
under a theory Plaintiff disclaimed. NCMEC closes by analyzing a count Plaintiff did not
supplement. The Opposition supplies no reason to deny the narrow supplementation Plaintiff
requested.

The Motion should be granted.

Date: August 26, 2026 Respectfully submitted,
